title: Cross-cycle SLI impact buckets and failover-budgeting for initiative prioritization
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: As initiatives span quarters, product and engineering teams struggle to prioritize reliability work because there is no standard, cross-cycle way to translate customer-visible risk into initiative priority. We frequently end up with parallel SLO improvements that compete for the same error-budget runway or with low-impact SLI regressions consuming disproportionate rollback attention. This ticket proposes a framework that buckets SLI issues by weighted customer-impact and attaches a small failover-budget per initiative group to enable safer rollouts and clearer prioritization.
background: Current state: teams use ad-hoc SLI dashboards and manual notes in initiative docs. Error budget pauses and rollbacks are decided in meetings with limited context. We lack a machine-readable score that combines user scale, incident cost, and SLI sensitivity. Similar efforts in other teams have used tokenized 'health credits' but were limited to single-cycle scopes.
objectives: Create a repeatable scoring model that maps SLI delta (e.g., p99 latency, success-rate) to customer-impact buckets (none/low/med/high) using traffic and revenue-weighted factors
Introduce a failover-budget allocation per initiative group (small percentage of global error budget) to authorize safe canary increases and controlled rollbacks
Expose the score and failover budget in Initiative Hub UI and the Initiative health export so PMs can filter and rank reliability work across cycles
Automate periodic recomputation so scores remain accurate across cross-cycle rollovers
acceptance_criteria: A scoring prototype exists and computes a repeatable score for at least 3 services across two example SLIs (p99 latency and request success-rate)
Failover-budget concept implemented as metadata attached to initiatives in the Initiative Hub data model
UI shows a sortable column 'Reliability Impact Score' and 'Failover Budget %' in the initiative list and initiative detail pages
A short runbook for how to consume failover budget during rollouts is published and linked from the initiative page
A dashboard card surfaces top 10 initiatives consuming failover budget and projected error-budget runway impact
proposed_solution: Data model: extend initiative schema with fields reliability_score (0-100) and failover_budget_pct (string percentage) and a human_readable_bucket label
Scoring formula: reliability_score = normalize(traffic_weight * sla_sensitivity + customer_value_weight * revenue_exposure + incident_history_weight * recent_incident_cost)
Failover allocation policy: default 2% of aggregated error budget per initiative group; can be adjusted by SRE leads during quarterly planning
Recompute cadence: nightly batch job that recomputes scores and flags delta > 10 points for review
UI/UX: add table column, detail pane widget with historical score timeline and link to runbook
Telemetry: emit events when failover budget is consumed > 50% for any initiative (for paging/escalation)
Rollout: pilot with three customer-facing services for 6 weeks, collect feedback, then iterate
milestones: 2026-03-15: Scoring prototype (data pipeline + formula) completed for pilot services
2026-04-01: Initiative schema extended and backend API endpoints ready
2026-04-15: UI wireframes validated with PMs and SREs; basic UI implemented

2026-06-01: Pilot retrospective and decision on org-wide rollout
2026-06-15: If approved, soft launch with auto-recompute enabled
success_metrics: Time-to-decision on reliability work reduced from median 10 days to 3 days (measured by initiative triage-to-commitment)
Number of cross-team meetings required for error-budget reconciliation cut by 50%
Less than 10% of initiatives exceed their failover budget during pilot
Post-rollout incidents tied to prioritized initiatives decrease by 20% quarter-over-quarter
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Score becomes a proxy that crowds out engineering judgment -> Mitigation: make scores advisory, require an SRE sign-off for any automated allocation changes
Risk: Incorrect traffic or revenue weights cause mis-prioritization -> Mitigation: surface the inputs in the UI and allow adjustment per product area
Risk: Failover budgets are gamed by teams -> Mitigation: emit audit logs and require post-consumption justification linked to incident reviews
Risk: Nightly recompute spikes causing churn -> Mitigation: threshold changes for UI alerts and backfill smoothing
implementation_notes: Prototype uses existing telemetry exports: p99 latency, success_rate, request_volume, and recent incident cost from observability ledger
We will store computed scores in Initiative Hub's existing metadata store to avoid schema migration complexity
